meetings.title: 12th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee members discussed “A Petition calling on the Government to establish general guidelines on grooming and dress codes for employees in the tourism industry, and urging the People’s Majlis to proceed with the resolution submitted to it and reach a decision on the matter”, has received the required number of signatures to meet threshold-1 as specified under Article 6-257(n)(1) of the Standing Orders of the People’s Majlis. It was further discussed that the resolution referred to in the petition is currently under consideration by the Economic Committee, and it was suggested that the committee’s progress on the matter should be reviewed. However, given the number of members present at the meeting, the required quorum for voting was not met. Therefore, Vaikaradhoo constituency member Hussain Ziyaadh, highlighted that the committee was unable to decide on the petition included in the agenda. The proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo constituency member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. He suggested that, in reviewing the progress made by the Economic Committee, a letter should be sent to the committee requesting information on the consultations held with the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation and the responses provided by the Ministry.

meetings.title: 10th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: During today’s meeting, the Committee discussed the petition titled “Petition to Pass the Amendment Proposed to Act No. 2010/7 (Decentralization Act) by the Honourable Member for Thulhaadhoo Constituency, Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru (2026/20/B.22)”, which had reached Threshold 1 in terms of the required number of signatures. Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed that the petition be referred to the Local Government Authority and the Decentralization Committee of the People’s Majlis for their comments. The proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. When put to a vote, the proposal was approved by a majority of the members present and participating in the vote. The Committee subsequently considered the petition titled “Petition Calling to Pass the Amendment Proposed to the Decentralization Act as Currently Proposed,” which had reached Threshold 2 in terms of the required number of signatures. Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed that the petition be referred to the Local Government Authority and the Decentralization Committee of the People’s Majlis for their comments, pursuant to Section 257-12(g) of the Standing Orders of the People’s Majlis. The proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. When put to a vote, the proposal was approved by a majority of the members present and participating in the vote. Furthermore, the Committee considered the petition calling for the withdrawal of the proposed amendment to the Decentralization Act. As comments from the Decentralization Committee of the People’s Majlis had not been sought in relation to this petition during the previous Committee meeting, Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed that the petition also be referred to the Decentralization Committee for its comments. The proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. When put to a vote, the proposal was approved by a majority of the members present and participating in the vote. As the final item on the agenda, the Committee discussed the review of the minimum number of signatures required for the respective petition thresholds, pursuant to Section 257-7(a) of the Standing Orders of the People’s Majlis. In this regard, Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed that no amendment be made to the percentages currently stipulated in Section 257-6(c) of the Standing Orders. The proposal was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. When put to a vote, the proposal was unanimously approved by the members present and participating in the vote.

meetings.title: 7th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee continued its work on reviewing the petitions submitted to the committee. First, before further discussions on the "Petition submitted regarding the prolonged and unresolved housing issue related to the K-Park Residences project," Vaikaradhoo Constituency Member Hussain Ziyadh proposed to send another letter to the Housing Committee to check the progress of the "Resolution submitted to ascertain the views of the Members of Parliament concerning the prolonged and unresolved issues faced in relation to the housing project started in Hulhumalé under the name of K-Park Residence," because the details regarding the Housing Committee's work on this resolution have not yet been received. meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee continued its work on reviewing the ongoing petitions currently at the committee. First, regarding the "Petition calling for a legal ban on the import, production, and sale of goods and materials in the Maldives from companies that fund and support Israel", Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to seek further clarification and information from the relevant state institutions. This was seconded by Komandoo Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim and passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. Next, the committee reviewed the "Petition regarding negligence in providing legally mandated benefits for children with disabilities." Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to conclude the work on this petition and inform the petitioners of the outcome, as the issues raised in the petition have now been resolved. This was seconded by Komandoo Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim and passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. After that, the committee reviewed the "Petition calling for solutions to the challenges faced by students studying in Spain under the government student loan scheme." As the issues highlighted in this petition have also been resolved, Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to conclude the work on the petition and notify the petitioners. This was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz and passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting. Lastly, the committee discussed the "Petition regarding the changes brought to the salaries of legal professionals working in councils and those under the Civil Service framework, following reforms to the National Pay Framework." Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to seek further information from the relevant state institutions regarding the matters raised in the petition. This was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed and passed unanimously by the members present at the time of voting.

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee first reviewed the response from the National Social Protection Agency (NSPA) concerning the "Petition regarding negligence in providing legally mandated benefits for children with disabilities." As the agency's response did not sufficiently address the specific information requested, Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed resending the inquiry to seek clear and comprehensive answers. This was seconded by Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed and was passed unanimously by the members present at the meeting. Next, the committee reviewed the "Petition calling for solutions to the challenges faced by students studying in Spain under the government student loan scheme". Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed proposed requesting the latest status update from the relevant Ministry before making a final decision. This was seconded by Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez and passed unanimously by the members present at the meeting. After that, the committee reviewed the "Petition regarding the prolonged and unresolved housing issues surrounding the K-Park Residencies project". Dhidhdhoo Constituency Member Abdul Latheef Mohamed proposed requesting details from the Housing Committee regarding their progress on the "Resolution to determine the Parliament's stance on the unresolved issues of the K-Park housing project in Hulhumalé." This was seconded by Central Hithadhoo Constituency Member Ahmed Azaan Marzooq and passed unanimously by the members present at the meeting. Lastly, the committee discussed the "Petition submitted to Parliament sharing the difficulties and concerns of persons with disabilities." Following deliberations, Vaikaradhoo Constituency Member Hussain Ziyad proposed seeking further clarification from relevant authorities regarding the specific measures they have taken to address the concerns raised in the petition. This was seconded by Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez and passed unanimously by the members present at the meeting.

meetings.title: 11th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the Committee first reviewed the petition submitted by civil employees of the Maldives Correctional Service. With reference to the discussions held with the Ministry of Finance and Planning and the Maldives Correctional Service, the Committee concluded that the National Pay Commission is currently working on the harmonization of salaries for state employees. This process is being implemented in phases, based on the fiscal capacity of the state. As employees are transitioned into the new pay structure, the concerns raised in the petition are expected to be addressed. Following this conclusion, Vaikaradhoo Constituency Member Hussain Ziyad proposed to inform the petitioners accordingly. The proposal was seconded by Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez. The proposal was unanimously passed by the members present at the meeting. Then the Committee reviewed the Petition for negligence in receiving statutory benefits for children with disabilities. Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to meet with Minsitry of Health to further review the issues highlighted in the Petition. This was seconded by Hinnavaru Constituency Member Mohamed Abdul Rahman. The proposal was unanimously passed by the members present at the meeting. The Committee then reviewed the petition regarding the prolonged and unresolved housing issues related to the K-Park Residencies project. As the People’s Majlis Committee on Housing is currently reviewing a resolution addressing the same concerns raised in the petition, Madaveli Constituency Member Mohamed Shameez proposed to defer the Petition Committee’s review until the Housing Committee concludes its review of the resolution. This proposal was seconded by Ungoofaaru Constituency Member Ibrahim Shifaz. The proposal was unanimously passed by the members present at the meeting. Lastly the Committee reviewed the Petition calling for a resolution to the challenges faced by students studying in Spain under the government’s student loan scheme. In regard to the petition, Vaikaradhoo Constituency Member Hussain Ziyad proposed to write to the Ministry of Higher Education, Labour and Skills Development to obtain up-to-date information on the matter. This was seconded by Komandoo Constituency Member Mohamed Ibrahim. The proposal was unanimously passed by the members present at the meeting.

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee discussed and decided on the working quorum of the committee as 4 members. This was proposed by Madaveli Constituency member Mohamed Shameez and seconded by North Dhidhdhoo Constituency member Abdul Latheef Mohamed. Secondly, the Committee decided on the voting quorum of the Committee. Madaveli Constituency member Mohamed Shameez proposed the voting quorum to be 7 members and North Henveyru Constituency member Ahmed Aifan seconded. Thirdly, the Committee decided on the working quorum for the summoned meetings mentioned under s.163 of the Standing Order of 19th Majlis as 7 members. This was proposed by North Henveyru Constituency member Ahmed and seconded by Velidhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Abbas. Furthermore, the members then decided on the Committee guidelines for the petitions submitted to the Committee. 1. Guidelines for Processing Eligible Petitions Submitted to the Committee: - The committee members unanimously agreed to adhere to the procedures established during the 19th Majlis while deliberating on such petitions. 2. Guidelines for Processing Ineligible Petitions Submitted to the Committee: - Velidhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Abbas proposed and North Hithadhoo Constituency Member Mohamed Sinan seconded that the petitioner be given the opportunity to resubmit the petition if the requirements mentioned in s.233 and s.234 of the Standing Orders are not met. - Furthermore, a procedural shift was implemented, allowing petitioners to make necessary amendments after submitting their petition to the Majlis. This adjustment eliminates the need for the committee's secretariats to assist in meeting petition requirements. - In addition, the Committee decided to send a memo to the General Administration Department of the People's Majlis outlining the petition requirements to ensure that the department meets them before referring a petition to the Committee.
